chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalhub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"When the mukatab (slave with a contract of manumission) becomes unable [to pay], his contract is not revoked back into slavery, but he is given a year or two; if he fulfills his contract, [he is freed], otherwise he is returned to slavery."

And if he had not done it, he would not have deserved punishment, nor would he have been transgressing regarding an obligation for which leaving it incurs sin; and that which clarifies also what we mentioned, that when the condition is fulfilled, he has the right to be returned to slavery, is what he narrated:

key_terms.الرِّقِّ: Slavery or the state of being a slave.
key_terms.الشَّرْطُ: The condition or term specified in the contract.
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave's manumission contract if he becomes unable to pay the agreed amount?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a compassionate grace period for the mukatab, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of easing hardship in financial contracts. It clarifies that the delay is a concession rather than a penalty, ensuring the slave is not immediately re-enslaved if he makes a good faith effort, thereby balancing the master's rights with the slave's dignity. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the fiqh of mukataba, emphasizing patience and leniency in debt collection.
